builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation
summary: CORAL replaces a monotonically growing agent context (as in ReAct-style loops) with an agent-callable toolset that checkpoints verified facts and resets the context to a clean state between episodes. The cost is added orchestration complexity, extra checkpointing calls, and a multi-episode reinforcement learning training stage if the full reported gains are wanted rather than only the prompt-level toolset. It can fail if the agent checkpoints incomplete or incorrect facts, since the discarded context is unrecoverable and errors then propagate across all subsequent episodes.
rationale: The checkpoint-and-reset toolset is implementable with a single GPU or API-based agents and the token savings directly address constrained budgets, but the accuracy gains depend on RL training and on the agent's checkpointing judgment, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.

claims.statement: CORAL replaces a monotonically growing agent context (as in ReAct-style loops) with an agent-callable toolset that checkpoints verified facts and resets the context to a clean state between episodes. The cost is added orchestration complexity, extra checkpointing calls, and a multi-episode reinforcement learning training stage if the full reported gains are wanted rather than only the prompt-level toolset. It can fail if the agent checkpoints incomplete or incorrect facts, since the discarded context is unrecoverable and errors then propagate across all subsequent episodes.
CORAL consumes 6-7x fewer input tokens than a ReAct agent while an 8B model reaches 42.8% average accuracy on GAIA, and improves a proprietary agent by 8.0 points on BrowseComp.
